name: Fiverr
tagline: A marketplace where you buy packaged freelance gigs: logos, edits, voiceovers, code, with escrow and reviews.

pricing.basis: free to browse, commission on transactions plus optional seller subscriptions
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You can build the software part of Fiverr in a day: gig listings, order states, messages, file delivery, a review table. What you cannot build is the several million sellers sitting on the other side of it at 3am willing to cut a logo for twenty dollars. The entire product is two-sided liquidity plus an escrow that makes strangers trust each other with money, and neither of those is a code problem. A personal replacement only makes sense if you already have your own freelancers, in which case you do not need a marketplace, you need a tracker. Build that instead and stop paying the commission on people you found yourself.
coreLoopDIY: A private brief-and-delivery tracker for freelancers you already know: create a job, set a rate and milestones, log messages and files, mark paid.
requirements: Freelancers you have already sourced yourself
Your own payment method for payouts, bank transfer, Wise, or Stripe payment links
Somewhere to run a local Node app
whatYouLose: Supply: thousands of sellers in every niche, available now, with sample work visible
Escrow and dispute resolution, so nobody has to trust anybody first
Cross-border payouts and tax paperwork handled for you
Reviews and order-completion history that make quality roughly guessable before you pay
Price discovery: knowing that a thing costs 25 dollars and not 400
moatNotes: Classic cold-start problem. The first version of your clone has zero sellers and zero buyers, and both sides only show up because the other side is already there.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay the Fiverr tax because it converts a vague need into a completed deliverable without a hiring process. The value is not the order form, it is the fact that ten people will bid on your thumbnail request within an hour, that you can see what they did for someone else, and that your money sits in escrow until files land. Commission is the price of not doing sourcing, vetting, contracting, and international payments yourself. Once you have found a person you trust, the marketplace stops earning its cut, which is exactly when a private tracker becomes the rational move.
notes: The order pipeline is an afternoon; the supply side is not. The moat is marketplace liquidity plus escrow: millions of sellers already standing there, and a trust layer that lets strangers transact sight unseen.
prompt:
Build a local-first freelancer job tracker called "Gigbook". It is NOT a marketplace: there is no discovery, no bidding, no public seller directory. It manages work with freelancers I already know.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15, App Router, TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/gigbook.db
- Tailwind CSS, no component library
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, single user, no auth, no telemetry, no external API calls

Data model:
- freelancer: id, name, contact (email or handle), skills (comma string), default_rate, currency, notes
- job: id, freelancer_id, title, brief (markdown text), agreed_amount, currency, status (draft | sent | in_progress | delivered | revising | accepted | paid | cancelled), due_date, created_at
- milestone: id, job_id, label, amount, due_date, done (bool), paid (bool)
- message: id, job_id, direction (out | in), body, created_at
- file: id, job_id, original_name, stored_path, uploaded_at (store uploads under ./data/uploads, stream from a route handler, no cloud storage)
- rating: id, job_id, quality 1-5, communication 1-5, would_rehire (bool), comment

Screens:
1. Dashboard: jobs grouped by status, total unpaid amount per currency, anything overdue flagged red
2. Freelancer list and detail: past jobs, average rating, total spent, rehire rate
3. Job detail: brief editor, milestone checklist with paid toggles, message log, file list with upload, status buttons that follow the pipeline
4. New job form that can prefill rate and currency from the chosen freelancer

Also include:
- A "brief" copy button that renders title, brief, milestones, amount, and due date as plain text ready to paste into email or chat
- CSV export of all jobs and payments at /api/export
- Seed script with two freelancers and three jobs across different statuses

Explicitly out of scope: payments processing, escrow, invoicing PDFs, contracts, email sending, multi-user accounts. If I later want payment links, I will paste a Stripe or Wise URL into a `payment_link` text field on the job, so add that field and render it as a link, nothing more.

Any secrets go in .env.example with no real values. Write a short README covering setup, the data file location, and how to back up ./data.
